question: Will US business AI use in the Census BTOS reach at least 35% in any month of 2027?
resolution_criteria: BTOS reports current use >=35% of firms
rationale: Diffusion has roughly doubled in two years from a low base; extrapolation is plausible but base effects fade
framework_relevance: Tests extensive-margin diffusion in a high-access, high-conversion economy
update_triggers: Major price declines; regulatory shocks; recession

question: Will at least 15% of euro-area firms report intense AI use by end-2028?
resolution_criteria: ECB repeat survey or equivalent shows intense-use share >=15%
resolution_source: ECB firm survey or published paper
rationale: Intense use is ~7% now and gated by complementary investment, which moves slowly
framework_relevance: Tests whether Europe moves from use to harvest
update_triggers: Cheaper inference; EU procurement push; power constraints

question: Will Canada's business AI use reach 20% by end-2028?
resolution_criteria: Official Canadian business survey shows share >=20%
resolution_source: Statistics Canada or official strategy tracker
rationale: Sovereign-AI strategy targets adoption but SME diffusion has lagged peers
framework_relevance: Tests whether a sovereign-AI strategy closes the conversion gap
update_triggers: Public compute rollout; training uptake; SME incentives

question: Will Italy's enterprise AI use exceed 25% by end-2030?
rationale: Italy starts near 8% with cited digital-skill gaps; catch-up requires sustained complement investment
framework_relevance: Tests the late-converter pathway in an advanced economy
update_triggers: Digital-skills changes; SME support; macro slowdown

question: Will US data centres consume at least 10% of US electricity by 2028?
rationale: LBNL range for 2028 is 6.7-12%; the top half of that range requires uninterrupted buildout
update_triggers: Chip availability; siting delays; efficiency gains

question: Will the accessible frontier task horizon exceed 8 hours at 50% success on a METR-like measure by end-2028?
resolution_criteria: Public evaluation reports >=8h 50%-horizon on a reproducible benchmark
rationale: Original draft extrapolated the post-2023 trend. Audit: METR current TH1.1 data report Claude Mythos Preview (early) at 1,044.8 minutes p50 (508.9-3,304.3), already above 8 hours, while warning that estimates above 16 hours are unreliable. Author must decide whether to resolve, rebase, or retire this question; the draft range is unchanged and remains hidden pending that decision.
framework_relevance: Direct x-axis test of capability progression
lower_bound_rationale: Retained unchanged from the draft; wide confidence intervals, task-suite sensitivity, and benchmark saturation argue against automatic upward revision.
upper_bound_rationale: Retained unchanged from the draft; the public threshold may already be crossed, so author review should resolve or redefine the question rather than silently revise probability.

question: Will open-weight models reach within 20% of leading closed models on a fixed-cost task bundle by end-2028?
rationale: Cost-adjusted gaps have compressed but frontier labs retain a training-compute edge
framework_relevance: Tests substitution between open access and closed access

question: Will worker-level GenAI adoption in Europe exceed 25% in the next EWCS-style cross-country release?
resolution_source: EWCS successor or harmonised official survey
rationale: Current average ~12% with wide country dispersion; workplace policy is loosening
framework_relevance: Tests use-stage steepening at the worker level

question: Will a major tax, customs, or benefits agency publish an audited result showing >=20% processing-time reduction from AI by end-2029?
resolution_criteria: Official audit or evaluation verifies >=20% reduction attributable to AI
rationale: Public-sector evidence is currently implementation-heavy and outcome-light everywhere
framework_relevance: Tests the state-capacity branch of the framework
update_triggers: Procurement changes; public backlash; audit publication

question: Will highly exposed entry-level cognitive occupations in at least one G7 economy show a >=5pp worse employment or hiring outcome than low-exposure peers by 2028?
resolution_criteria: Official labour/posting data with transparent exposure grouping show differential >=5pp
rationale: Early relative-softness signals exist but attribution against the macro cycle is hard
framework_relevance: Tests distribute-stage concentration of adjustment costs
update_triggers: Macro recession; immigration changes; labour regulation
